item.text:
**Assessment**
Mixed, leaning yes on economic intent and design, but not cleanly on execution. In 2024 Abiy’s government clearly pursued macro reform, private-sector opening, debt stabilization, and safety nets. The main counterweight is that conflict, emergency rule, and leverage-seeking moves undercut the credibility of “broad-based, sustainable prosperity” and point more toward regime management than fully development-first politics.

**Accepted claims**
- **IMF approves four-year US$3.4 billion ECF for Ethiopia** | International Monetary Fund | 2024-07-29 | [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/29/pr24291-ethiopia-imf-exec-board-approves-4yr-us3b-ecf-arr)  
  The IMF said the program supports Ethiopia’s Homegrown Economic Reform Agenda, aims to restore external debt sustainability, and is designed to promote higher, more inclusive, private-sector-led growth. It also emphasizes social safety nets, fiscal discipline, and better governance rather than short-term distributional politics.  
  QIDs: 5B.1, 4B.10

- **World Bank backs Ethiopia’s reforms to promote sustainable and inclusive growth** | World Bank | 2024-07-30 | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/07/30/world-bank-backs-ethiopia-s-reforms-to-promote-sustainable-and-inclusive-afe-growth)  
  The World Bank said the reform package aims to make the economy more inclusive, expand the private sector’s role, improve fiscal transparency, strengthen SOE performance, and expand social safety nets for poor and vulnerable households. That is strong positive evidence for broad-based prosperity as an explicit objective.  
  QIDs: 5B.1, 4B.10

- **Ethiopia signs 1.72 billion USD financing agreements with the World Bank** | Ministry of Finance, Ethiopia | 2024-04-05 | [URL](https://www.mofed.gov.et/blog/ethiopia-signs-172-billion-usd-financing-agreements-with-the-world-bank/)  
  The agreements funded rural connectivity, food security, adaptive safety nets, and other development projects aimed at sustainable development and inclusive growth. This is concrete execution evidence that points toward broader welfare rather than narrow elite payoff.  
  QIDs: 5B.1

- **IMF reaches staff-level agreement on the first review of Ethiopia’s ECF** | International Monetary Fund | 2024-09-27 | [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24348-ethiopia-imf-reaches-agreement-on-the-first-review-of-the-extended-credit-facility)  
  IMF staff said the reform program was advancing well, the exchange-rate regime had largely normalized official/parallel gaps, and maintaining reform momentum would support macro stability and stronger growth. The same release stresses continued social safety nets and domestic revenue mobilization, which fits a sustainability-oriented agenda.  
  QIDs: 5B.1, 4B.10

- **Landlocked Ethiopia signs pact to use Somaliland’s Red Sea port** | Reuters, republished by MarketScreener | 2024-01-01 | [URL](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Landlocked-Ethiopia-signs-pact-to-use-Somaliland-s-Red-Sea-port-45654814/)  
  Reuters treated the Berbera MOU as leverage-seeking and destabilizing, because it tied port access to possible recognition and naval use. This is negative evidence against a purely prosperity-first approach, since it looks more like geopolitical bargaining than patient, broad-based development.  
  QIDs: 5B.1, 4B.10

- **The state-of-emergency proclamation centralized coercive authority** | ENA English | 2024-11-03 | [URL](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/en_30124)  
  The proclamation centralized authority under an operation command, restricted CSOs and media suspected of aiding “terrorist” groups, and empowered replacement of local administrators. That is not direct economic evidence, but it does suggest the government kept prioritizing control and regime security over an environment of durable broad-based prosperity.  
  QIDs: 5B.1, 4B.8, 4B.9, 4B.10, 4B.4, 4B.6

- **Authorities suspended three rights groups while Abiy praised reforms** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-12-02 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/ethiopia-authorities-suspend-three-rights-groups)  
  HRW described a pattern of selective punishment of watchdogs alongside reform rhetoric. That is weak but relevant negative evidence: it suggests political control was still being used to manage the environment rather than relying purely on broad-based, durable prosperity gains.  
  QIDs: 5B.1, 4B.4, 4B.5, 4B.6, 4B.10

**Search gap**
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence of classic rent extraction or direct patronage buying in the available reporting.
- The negative side is therefore mostly indirect: conflict, emergency centralization, and leverage-seeking behavior that undercut sustainable prosperity rather than proving a detailed rent-seeking program.
